problems.key_observation: The sequence of exponents a_k encodes a lattice walk whose group-theoretic product can be reduced via induction or geometric/topological arguments, ultimately forcing commutativity.
problems.solution_architecture: The proof proceeds by induction on m+n, handling base cases directly. For larger parameters, it reduces the problem either by reparameterizing (m > n) or by dualizing (m < n), using arithmetic properties of the sequence a_k. Each approach ultimately reduces the group relation to a commutator, forcing gh = hg.

solution_archetypes: Periodicity via modular arithmetic and pigeonhole principle
problems.key_observation: The sequence can be expressed as x_n = cos(F_n b), where F_n is the Fibonacci sequence and b is chosen so that a = cos b; this links the recurrence to periodicity via modular properties of the Fibonacci numbers.
problems.solution_architecture: First, rule out the case |a|>1 by showing the sequence cannot reach zero. Then, for |a|≤1, express the sequence in terms of cos(F_n b) using induction, leveraging trigonometric identities and the Fibonacci sequence. If x_n=0, deduce that b is a rational multiple of π, so the sequence of (F_n b) modulo 2π is periodic. Use modular arithmetic and the pigeonhole principle to conclude periodicity of the sequence.

problems.solution_architecture: Reduce injectivity to monotonicity of a real-valued function along any line segment between two points.
